sdkVersionAtPass._note: 0.2.9 changed NO pin. These are the versions the skin was measured against and built on; recorded because the skin overrides tokens that @civitai/theme declares and @property-registers, so a theme bump is the thing most able to move it out from under us.
sdkVersionAtPass._measured: read from each installed package's own version field after `npm ci` in a worktree off origin/main. A find for a @civitai package nested UNDER another package's node_modules returned ZERO -- worth re-running after any bump, because the design-system skill records a nested older @civitai/components silently shadowing the hoisted newer one via a shared injection marker.

decisions.what: the SDK pins were bumped in their OWN PR, ahead of the pass
decisions.chose: two PRs -- #13 (pins only, no production code) then #14 (the pass)
decisions.because: operator fork, answered explicitly. Phase 0 measured the pins four-plus minors behind (app-sdk 0.27.0 against 0.37.0, blocks-react 0.36.0 against 0.47.0), which made ResourceCard and the pre-handshake theme read unavailable AS PINNED. Bumping inside the pass would have put a dependency jump and a redesign in one diff, so a post-merge regression could not be attributed to either. The split earned itself immediately: the bump surfaced a REQUIRED new field on SharedListItem that `npm test` stayed green through (367/367) while `tsc --noEmit` failed -- vitest does not typecheck, so the test tier alone would have shipped it.

decisions.what: the `Popular right now` rail is THRESHOLDED rather than relabelled or left alone
decisions.chose: render nothing below POPULAR_MIN_PLAYS 2 AND POPULAR_MIN_ENTRIES 3, with no copy explaining the absence
decisions.because: operator fork, answered explicitly. Measured live 2026-09-05, the five cards under that heading read 6, 1, 1, 1, 1 plays -- four of five tied at the minimum possible non-zero value, on the most prominent surface after the title. One play cannot distinguish 'people like this' from 'the author opened it once'; one or two cards is a list with a superlative over it, not a ranking. An explanatory line was rejected in the same breath: it would re-raise exactly the thing the threshold suppresses, and the Discover grid below is a complete front door on its own.

decisions.what: the filter runs BEFORE the entry count, not after
decisions.chose: filter to qualifying entries, then require the count
decisions.because: the other order lets six one-play entries satisfy the entry floor and render a rail in which nothing clears the play floor -- i.e. it would make POPULAR_MIN_PLAYS decorative. Pinned by its own test ('does NOT let sub-floor entries pad the set up to the entry floor').

decisions.what: PopularRail filters ITSELF instead of trusting its caller
decisions.chose: call popularRailEntries inside the component that renders the heading
decisions.because: the heading makes a claim only the data can honour, so the component that renders the claim is the one that checks it. A caller cannot forget, and a future second caller inherits the guarantee.

decisions.what: an empty collection is DISABLED, not hidden
decisions.chose: disabled card with a label that says why ('<name> -- nothing to play yet')
decisions.because: measured live: 'Bookmarked Articles - 0 items' rendered an ordinary play affordance, so the one thing this app exists to do silently did nothing -- indistinguishable from the app being broken. Hiding it would be a second lie: the viewer put that collection in their own list and would find it missing.

decisions.what: the sort hint moved out of the chip row and became a sentence
decisions.chose: 'Sorted by most followed.' on its own line, and the duplicate title= tooltip deleted
decisions.because: at 12px dimmed inline after two chips, the bare 'Most followed' read as a THIRD, DISABLED sort option -- a claim about the control surface, not about the sort. A sentence with a full stop cannot be mistaken for a chip. The same string was also the Popular button's native tooltip, delivering it twice by two mechanisms; the test now asserts the tooltip's ABSENCE, so dropping one delivery cannot let it drift back.

decisions.what: release 0.2.7, not 0.3.0
decisions.chose: follow this repo's patch-bump convention
decisions.because: gen-matrix went 0.8.9 -> 0.9.0 partly to dodge an ambiguity -- 0.8.10 is greater under semver and LESS under lexicographic comparison, and nothing documents which `civitai app submit` implements. 0.2.7 is unambiguous under both, so no escape hatch was needed and the repo's own run (0.2.3 through 0.2.6, all patch bumps carrying features) stands. The floor was read from the NO-ARG listing, because constraints 13 records THIS app returning a withdrawn row for a version that was live.

decisions.what: the store description was re-read against the change rather than assumed unaffected
decisions.chose: no copy change
decisions.because: block.manifest.json tells users 'a Popular rail builds out of those votes as more people use the app' -- a claim about the exact surface this pass changed. It survived, and got MORE accurate: the rail used to appear after a SINGLE play, which that sentence did not describe. Recorded because nothing checks this, and a release that silently invalidates its own store copy is the easy miss.

decisions.what: brandDepth moved `accent` -> `skin`
decisions.chose: the app owns both palettes; the platform owns neither
decisions.because: operator feedback round 3 item 5, answered explicitly. This is the deferred phase-1 entry being taken up, not a new idea. It closes that entry in the direction the entry anticipated -- it said whoever lands a colour literal owns the dual-theme assertions, and this pass lands 28 of them and writes the assertions.

decisions.what: the skin redefines the --civitai-* TOKENS rather than re-pointing components at an app-local palette
decisions.chose: override the token values under [data-pc-skin][data-theme...]
decisions.because: measured: eight components reference var(--civitai-color-*) DIRECTLY rather than going through theme.ts's palette() (App, CollectionGrid, CollectionViewer, ModeSwitcher, TipModal, toast, ...). Re-pointing each is eight diffs that drift apart, and would still leave every @civitai/blocks-react/ui component (Button/Alert/Card/Modal) on the platform's blue -- the pack beside the app instead of part of it. One override skins all of it. Verified in a real engine, not inferred: headless chromium reports --civitai-color-primary as rgb(250,100,120) and the outline Button's border as the same, so the pack IS taking the app's palette.

decisions.what: the token overrides are UNLAYERED while index.css is wrapped in `@layer app`
decisions.chose: opposite treatment for the two halves of the app CSS, in two separate files
decisions.because: unlayered declarations beat layered ones outright, and that cuts both ways. The tokens must beat @civitai/theme, which is itself unlayered (measured: zero `@layer` in @civitai/theme@0.3.1), so a layered override would be silently INERT -- they win on specificity instead, (0,2,0) against the package's (0,1,0). index.css must NOT beat @civitai/components, which ships inside `@layer civitai.components` and reaches this app at runtime via injectBlocksStyles(); an unlayered reset there is the design system's most-repeated gotcha. Merging the two files breaks one of them whichever way it goes.

decisions.what: the layer ORDER statement lives in index.html, not in a bundled stylesheet
decisions.chose: `@layer app, civitai.components;` as the first CSS in the inline <style>
decisions.because: layer rank is fixed by FIRST ENCOUNTER, and @civitai/components arrives at RUNTIME. If the pack injected before the app's order statement was parsed, `civitai.components` would rank BELOW `app` and the reset would win after all -- the same defect reached by a different route, and invisible to any test of the CSS files alone. An inline <style> in <head> is parsed before any script runs, which is the only position that cannot lose that race.

decisions.what: light theme does NOT use the brand plate as its primary
decisions.chose: #FA6478 in dark, #C8324B (the same hue, driven down in lightness) in light
decisions.because: white on #FA6478 is 2.35:1 -- a filled primary button in light theme could not carry its own label. The brand kit's own tonal rule (one hue at different lightnesses, never a second hue) is what makes the substitute legitimate rather than a second brand. Dark keeps the plate exactly, so the mark and the UI agree there; skin.test.ts pins BOTH facts, including the 2.35:1 that forces the split.

decisions.what: the page background moved from `surface-2` to `body`
decisions.chose: page = body, card = surface, recess = surface-2
decisions.because: under `accent` this was arbitrary -- the platform's light theme made all three the same colour, so nothing distinguished them and dark's surface-2 being the LIGHTER value went unnoticed. Giving the three tokens three real values turns it into an actual decision, and leaving it would have made the page the brightest plane with every card a hole punched in it.

decisions.what: the boot skeleton literals were re-sourced from skin.css, and bootTokens.test.ts with them
decisions.chose: repoint the existing parity test at src/skin.css instead of @civitai/theme
decisions.because: the coupled surface a skin pass is most likely to miss, because it lives in a different file and its test stays GREEN. index.html hardcodes boot colours (a var cannot be used before the stylesheet loads) and that suite asserted them against the INSTALLED package. The skin overrides those same tokens, so left as-is every assertion still passed while the viewer got a platform-grey boot that snapped to rose at handoff. Mutant M10 confirms the repointed test catches exactly that.

decisions.what: the mark was added to the browse header, with theme-INVARIANT colours
decisions.chose: inline SVG copied from brand/icon.svg, aria-hidden, never token-driven
decisions.because: under `accent` the brand lived only in the store assets; `skin` is what earns it a place in the UI. Its fills are deliberately NOT tokens -- the same call `stage` makes for the player chrome: a mark is an identity and must be the same rose in both themes, or it stops matching the store icon in one of them. brandMark.test.ts asserts the component against the vector AND against the hue written in brand/README.md, so an edit to both files still has to disagree with the kit.

decisions.what: the %-split tip, follow via the host bridge, hide-badges-but-keep-balance, and keeping Most Followers
decisions.chose: recorded here as operator forks; NONE implemented in 0.2.9
decisions.because: owed from round 3 and previously unrecorded -- they lived only in a handoff doc, which is the medium this ledger exists to outlive. They are upstream work (civitai/civitai + civitai-app-starters) and are ranked separately; writing them down is not shipping them. The %-split tip in particular carries five design hazards, none cheaply discoverable at runtime -- partial failure across two transactions, TIP_MIN per leg, TIP_MAX_PER_TIP applying PER LEG so one click could send 10,000 against a store description promising 5,000, self-tip 403 when curator == viewer, and the app-local daily allowance needing to debit both legs.

decisions.what: the skin also overrides the four --civitai-color-gray-* tokens the PACK consumes
decisions.chose: gray-1/2/5 invariant in the base block; gray-9 theme-varying
decisions.because: an adversarial audit refuted the claim that overriding tokens 'skins the app and the pack together'. It did not: @civitai/components reaches PAST the semantic tokens into the theme-INVARIANT gray ramp, which this skin was not overriding, and a pack Slider track measured rgb(233,236,239) -- the platform's cold blue-grey -- on the rose light surface. Only four ramp tokens are referenced by components@0.4.1 + blocks-react@0.47.0 (re-derived, and the coverage guard now scans BOTH packages so the set cannot grow silently). gray-1/2/5 stay invariant, matching upstream's own semantics, and light inherits them because a light root also matches the base selector.

decisions.what: gray-9 is the one ramp token this skin makes THEME-VARYING
decisions.chose: dark #f4e9ec / light #231017, i.e. it co-varies with primary-fg
decisions.because: the pack's tooltip is `background: gray-9; color: primary-fg`. Upstream that is always safe because primary-fg is #fefefe in both themes. This skin cannot keep that: our primary is a light rose, so dark's primary-fg has to be a near-black (#2a0611) to carry 6.3:1 on it -- and near-black on the platform's dark gray-9 measures 1.20:1, an invisible tooltip. No Tooltip renders in this app today, so it was LATENT rather than broken; it is pinned anyway, because 'we do not use that component yet' is not a property anyone re-checks. Re-measured in a browser after the fix: 15.64:1 dark, 18.14:1 light.

decisions.what: the third way this skin could ship inert -- main.tsx simply not importing it
decisions.chose: a guard that reads main.tsx with COMMENTED LINES STRIPPED
decisions.because: the audit commented out `import './skin.css'` and the full suite stayed green at 436/436, both tiers: the app would have shipped with every surface reverted to platform blue-grey, no console error. Every other guard reads CSS off disk and jsdom applies no CSS, so the one line that makes the skin reach a browser was unpinned -- while the commit title asserted 'the two ways a skin ships inert'. 🔴 The FIRST version of the new guard searched the file for the string './skin.css' and therefore PASSED its own mutant, because `// import './skin.css';` still contains the word: a guard on a WORD, walkable by rewording. It now strips line comments and is killed by both the comment-out and the delete shape.

deferred.what: phase 1 (brand) -- DONE in 0.2.9, no longer deferred
deferred.why: closed by this pass. The entry's condition was mechanical -- grepping src/theme.ts for a hex literal and expecting a non-zero count -- and it is worth recording that the condition AS WRITTEN would not have fired: theme.ts is still literal-free, because the skin puts its literals in src/skin.css and theme.ts still resolves through var(). The SPIRIT fired exactly as intended: a colour literal landed in the app, and whoever landed it owed the dual-theme assertions. They are written (src/skin.test.ts, both themes) and mutation-checked.
deferred.closingCondition: CLOSED 2026-09-06 at 0.2.9. A future re-open needs a new entry, not this one.
deferred._lesson: a closing condition pinned to a FILE PATH can be satisfied by relocation. Prefer one pinned to the property -- 'a colour literal exists anywhere the app renders from' -- over one pinned to a path.

deferred.what: phase 3 (interaction) -- the recorded condition is MET; the phase itself is still not run
deferred.why: the condition was 'an --evidence capture of the PLAYER states is taken and its a11y section read'. Done: the capture recipe gained a `player` state (talos-infra 5825b698f) and the phase-0 baseline reports player 89 elements / 29 unique testids / a11y violations 0 (interactive-name 0, img-alt 0, control-label 0, heading-order 0), console 0, failed network 0 of 24, state `populated` -- so the zeros are not the empty-state artefact the recipe warns about. Recorded honestly: a11y-violations-zero is NOT the same claim as 'reduced-motion, optimistic rollback and menu semantics are correct', which is what phase 3 actually audits. The condition was weaker than the phase it was attached to. It is met; the phase is not.

Whoever writes those tests checks it. Nothing in this repo measures them today.

deferred.why: no measured defect. The app already renders the viewer's own handle rather than 'you' ('by zachlowdenzx' on the viewer's own cards), which is the phase-4 rule this pass would have been checking.
deferred.closingCondition: ends if a capture ever shows the string 'you' or 'You' as a curator/author label -- `grep -c '>You<'` over a captured DOM is the check. No action needed while that is 0.

deferred.what: phase 5 (moderation) not run -- the app has no report/escalation affordance
deferred.why: unlike custom-generators, this app publishes NO user-authored text or media of its own. Its shared-storage writes are play VOTES keyed by collectionId -- ids, not content -- and every image shown is an existing public Civitai image already under platform moderation. There is no app-owned surface for a viewer to report.
deferred.closingCondition: ends if this app ever writes user-authored TEXT to shared storage (a title, a note, a caption). The mechanical check is whether SharedAppendValue's `title` field is ever populated from user input rather than from a collection name -- `git grep -n 'append(' src/lib/popular.ts` and read the call site. Whoever adds such a field owns the abuse seam.

deferred.what: phase 7 (re-shoot) not run in this pass either
deferred.why: phase 7 trails phase 8 by construction -- the re-shoot needs the new version LIVE, i.e. through moderator review. The previous entry here named 0.2.7 / 9e17c32 and was STALE within a day (0.2.8 shipped and went live); this one names the version it was written for, so its staleness is at least legible. The phase-0 --evidence baseline for THIS pass already exists and is durable: civit/captures/pc-0208-verify/phase0-before/ (discover / mine / player), captured against live 0.2.8.
deferred.closingCondition: ends when 0.2.9 reads approved/live with this PR's squash sha on the NO-ARG listing, AND an --evidence capture of all three states is diffed against phase0-before/ with evidence.py diff. That diff is the taste delta and the only part of this pass that is evidence rather than opinion. Whoever cuts the capture checks it.

brand.hueFromSystem: pass -- #FA6478 read from brand/README.md and brand/icon.svg; brandMark.test.ts asserts the component against BOTH, so agreeing with one is not enough
brand.heroReproducible: n-a -- no hero image generated this pass; no Buzz spent
brand.dualTheme: pass -- 32 token values, every surface/border/text pair asserted in BOTH themes by src/skin.test.ts, plus the PACK pairings the skin can break without touching either file (tooltip bubble, slider track). Mutants M7 (light-only) and M8 (dark-only) each go red in ONE theme, which is what shows the per-theme assertions bite separately rather than as one blanket check.
brand.noHardcodedThemeColour: pass for the app's own surfaces, and the earlier wording here OVERCLAIMED -- corrected after an audit. The app owns 32 theme literals, all confined to src/skin.css. Colour literals also live in SEVEN other files: Maturity.tsx, CollectionGrid.tsx, Player.tsx, CollectionViewer.tsx, components/styles.ts, toast.tsx, ModeSwitcher.tsx. Most are media-overlay chrome under the same rationale as theme.ts `stage` -- they must read against arbitrary user media, not against a page background -- but they are neither IN `stage` nor individually documented, so the previous claim ('the only colours outside it are ... the stage chrome and the brand mark') read as coverage it did not have. One is arguably now WRONG and is recorded rather than changed: Maturity.tsx's badge is rgba(224,49,49,0.92) = #e03131, @civitai/theme's DARK-THEME ERROR value, i.e. a platform red inside an all-rose palette. It sits on media rather than on an app surface so the clash is slight, and restyling a maturity badge is a product decision with no measurement behind it.

interaction.reducedMotion: not-measured -- see deferred phase 3; this pass added no new motion

tests.regressionWatchedRed: pass -- round 2: 16 mutants (the original 11 plus one per audit finding), all killed by ASSERTION, each naming its own guard, byte-identical restore after each, with a baseline control confirming the unmutated tree green.
tests.survivorsFound: 3 across two rounds, and none was simply a missing test. (1) Round 1: M6 was UNREACHABLE -- it renamed the very block skin.test.ts looks up at import time, so the module threw before the compound-selector guard executed; the suite went red and the mutant LOOKED killed while the guard was untested. Rebuilt to ADD a bare block. The battery's own kill-detector was wrong in the same round (counting only assertion lines scored an import failure as SURVIVED -- a reassuring zero) and was fixed to report the two apart. (2) Round 2, found by an external audit, not by me: commenting out the skin import kept 436/436 green. (3) The guard written to close (2) then SURVIVED its own mutant, because it asserted the WORD './skin.css' and `// import './skin.css';` still contains it -- spelled rather than structural. Now strips line comments; killed by both the comment and delete shapes.
tests.suite: 398 -> 444 (+46: skin.test.ts 38, skinRoot.test.tsx 3, brandMark.test.ts 5); both vitest projects green
tests.beyondTheSuite: the load-bearing claims are about the CSS CASCADE, which jsdom does not implement, so a green unit suite could not settle them. Measured in headless chromium against a production-shaped bundle, twice -- once for the original claims and again after the audit fixes, because an audit fix resets the verification gate. (1) The skin beats @civitai/theme despite the package's sheet being injected LATER: --civitai-color-body rgb(18,9,12) dark / rgb(251,241,243) light, radius .625rem, the pack's outline Button border rgb(250,100,120). (2) `@layer app` genuinely protects the pack -- a Preflight-style `* { border-width: 0 }` INSIDE the layer leaves the Button at 1px, the SAME rule unlayered takes it to 0px, shipped baseline 1px. That control had to be ADDED, because the reset this app ships contains nothing that could strip a pack style: the layer is PREVENTIVE, and the control is what separates 'the layer works' from 'nothing was threatening it'. (3) After the ramp fix: pack Slider / SegmentedControl / Image backgrounds carry NO platform grey in either theme (leak set empty), and the tooltip pairing reads 15.64:1 dark / 18.14:1 light against the 1.20:1 it would have shipped. 🔴 One honest detail from that run: the SegmentedControl resolves to surface-2, not to gray-1, because blocks-react's own UNLAYERED interactive stylesheet overrides the pack's layered rule -- so the gray-1 override is defensive, not load-bearing.
tests.flakeObserved: one pre-existing test unrelated to this pass -- App.test.tsx 'appends the next page on sentinel intersection and dedupes the re-emitted id' -- failed once in the first full-suite run and then passed 3/3 in isolation and 3/3 more full-suite runs. Not touched by this diff; recorded rather than re-run away. It is an IntersectionObserver timing dependency, and the durable fix is to remove the timing dependency, not to retry.
tests.auditRound: one external adversarial round at 460598ba2, dispatched blind against the diff. Three 🟡 findings, all coverage rather than behaviour, all fixed here and each re-verified by its own mutant: the layered-index.css guard was half-blind to a rule appended AFTER the layer block (greedy `[\s\S]*` backtracking to the file's last `\n}`); the skin import was unpinned; and the pack's gray-ramp consumption was outside the coverage scan. The audit also independently re-derived the suite delta, the cascade measurements and the contrast matrix, and could NOT reproduce round 1's specific 11-mutant table -- it built its own 8-mutant battery instead, which is the correct response to a self-reported table.
